item.title: Electron spin unlocks magnetic control of hydrogen surface reactions
item.description: Chemical reactions at surfaces play a central role in many processes, including catalysis and materials synthesis. It is well known that the outcome of these reactions is influenced by the translational, vibrational and rotational motions of atoms and molecules. Now, a study shows that electron spin, another fundamental property of matter, also influences how chemical reactions at surfaces unfold. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Heavy water's atmospheric fingerprints boost weather forecasts for up to five days
item.description: Weather forecasts rely on many different kinds of data, including temperature, humidity and wind. For the first time, researchers, including those at the University of Tokyo, have demonstrated that a long-theorized improvement to weather models—adding data on water isotopes in the atmosphere—does work. They showed that incorporating satellite measurements of water vapor isotopes into weather models improves forecasts of atmospheric conditions for up to five days, including predictions of heavy rainfall in many regions. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In 2010, US scientists tracked dye 41.2 miles in Montana’s Missouri River; a reservoir held it 8.2 hours
item.description: Scientists conducted a dye-tracing experiment on Montana's Missouri River. This study examined how substances move through the waterway over forty miles.
